_comment_input_source: Select 'rtsp', 'usb', or 'file' for your input source
_comment_device_id: Device identifier for MQTT messages. Leave empty to auto-detect from MAC address

runtime._comment_skip_frames: Frame skipping per model. Value = process every Nth frame: 0 or 1 = every frame (no skipping), 2 = every 2nd frame (half the work), 3 = every 3rd, etc. Higher value = lower NPU/CPU load and less heat, but fewer detections per second (slower reaction to movement). See _frame_skip_notes below for guidance.

_comment_log_dir: Directory for the rotating structured log (gaze.log, 5MB x 5 files). Default '/tmp' (RAM/tmpfs) is robust against delayed SD-card mount at boot. Use an SD path (e.g. '/storage/sd/logs') only if you need logs to persist across reboots. See _log_notes below.

_input_source_notes.note: Set input_source to your desired input type. Configure all three sources so you can easily switch between them
_input_source_notes.usage: Change 'input_source' value to switch between inputs without editing URLs/paths

_input_source_priority_notes.description: Controls where video input configuration is read from
_input_source_priority_notes.config: Use 'input' section from this config.json file (default, easier for deployment)
_input_source_priority_notes.registry: Use BrightSign registry value 'bsext-gaze-video-device' (flexible for runtime changes)
_input_source_priority_notes.priority: CLI args > [config or registry based on this setting] > [other] > auto-detect
_input_source_priority_notes.note: Set to 'config' to use config.json, or 'registry' to use BrightSign registry

_test_mode_notes.description: Test mode configuration for debugging individual models
_test_mode_notes.test_face_only: Set to true to run ONLY RetinaFace (disable YOLOX). Default: false
_test_mode_notes.test_yolo_only: Set to true to run ONLY YOLOX (disable RetinaFace). Default: false
_test_mode_notes.note: Both can be false (default) to run both models in parallel on separate NPU cores (production mode)
_test_mode_notes.usage: See TEST_MODES.md for detailed usage examples and debugging workflows

_frame_skip_notes.description: Per-model frame skipping to reduce NPU/CPU load. Located under "runtime": face_skip_frames (RetinaFace) and yolo_skip_frames (YOLOX).
_frame_skip_notes.how_it_works: The worker processes 1 out of every N frames and skips the rest. Skipped frames are still captured but not run through the model, so they cost almost nothing.

values.0 or 1: Process every frame - maximum accuracy/responsiveness, highest load (default)
values.2: Process every 2nd frame - roughly halves that model's NPU + CPU work
values.3: Process every 3rd frame - roughly one third of the work
values.N: Process every Nth frame - effective inference rate becomes (capture_fps / N)

_frame_skip_notes.effect: Higher value => lower CPU/NPU usage, lower power/heat, smoother host playback, BUT fewer detections per second and slower reaction to fast movement. Detections are simply reused/absent between processed frames.

tuning_guidance.single_core_npu: On single-NPU-core SoCs (e.g. LS5/RK3568) both models share one NPU and serialize. Skipping the pricier model (YOLOX) frees the NPU so the other model (RetinaFace) also speeds up. Start with yolo_skip_frames=2.
tuning_guidance.multi_core_npu: On 3-core NPU SoCs (e.g. XT5/RK3588) each model has its own core; skipping is usually unnecessary unless CPU (pre/resize/visualization) is the limit.
tuning_guidance.people_counting: People/faces move slowly relative to 30fps, so yolo_skip_frames=2 or 3 rarely misses anyone while cutting load significantly.
tuning_guidance.measure: Enable log_performance=true and compare the PERF log lines (npu/total ms and fps) before and after changing these values.

_frame_skip_notes.example: face_skip_frames=0, yolo_skip_frames=2  => RetinaFace every frame, YOLOX every 2nd frame.

options.debug: Most verbose - all logs including DEBUG messages (use for development/troubleshooting)
options.info: General information - INFO, WARN, ERROR, and CRITICAL messages (recommended default)
options.warn: Warnings and errors only - WARN, ERROR, and CRITICAL messages (production mode)
options.error: Errors only - ERROR and CRITICAL messages (minimal logging)

_log_level_notes.note: Change log_level without recompiling. Logs are written to log_dir location.

_log_notes.description: Log file layout on the player.
_log_notes.structured_log: log_dir/gaze.log (default /tmp/gaze.log) - the main application log. Rotates automatically at 5MB, keeping 5 files (gaze.log, gaze.log.1 .. gaze.log.4). Grep this for PERF, detections, errors, etc.
_log_notes.console_log: /tmp/gaze_console.log - raw stdout/stderr capture (early-boot messages, crashes). Truncated on each start. Not rotated; kept small.
_log_notes.why_tmp: /tmp is tmpfs (RAM). Logging here avoids losing logs when the SD card mount is delayed at boot. Downside: logs are cleared on reboot/power-cycle.
_log_notes.persistent: Set log_dir to an SD path (e.g. /storage/sd/logs) to keep logs across reboots, accepting the boot-time mount-race risk.

_blur_faces_notes.description: Person blurring for privacy protection in output frames (blurs entire person bounding box)
_blur_faces_notes.defaults: All blur settings are optional. Defaults: blur_faces=false, blur_method=pixelate, blur_intensity=12
_blur_faces_notes.blur_faces: Set to true to enable person blurring (default: false)

blur_method.gaussian: Smooth blur effect (currently configured) - use kernel size >= 71 for effective anonymization

blur_intensity.pixelate: Block size in pixels (4-32). Smaller = more detail visible. Default: 12
blur_intensity.gaussian: Kernel size (31-99, must be odd). Larger = more blur. Currently: 71

_blur_faces_notes.note: Blur is applied to entire person bounding box (full body), affecting output images written to output_dir
_blur_faces_notes.minimal_config: To enable with defaults, just add: "blur_faces": true
